newsitem.title: FRANCE: Power workers on strike in latest French unrest.
newsitem.headline: Power workers on strike in latest French unrest.

text.p: French electricity and gas workers staged a 24-hour strike on Tuesday over feared job losses as unrest partly inspired by concessions to striking truck drivers hit oil refineries and public transport in two cities.

About half the 140,000 workers at the state EDF-GDF electricity and gas utility heeded the strike call, cutting power output and forcing electricity imports from Britain, Spain and Portugal, unions said.

The stoppage, coinciding with talks by European Union energy ministers in Brussels, is to protest at EU liberalisation plans and feared job cuts. There were also wildcat power cuts in the northern city of Rouen, unions said.
A spokesman for EDF had no news of cuts but said the stoppage seemed to have fairly strong support.

"While 15,000 jobs have been cut over the past 10 years at EDF-GDF, (management) is pushing to cut another 15,000 over five years," said Jean-Marc Mauchauffee of the pro-Socialist CFDT union. "We want shorter working hours to create jobs."
Unions were also due to march in Paris later on Tuesday to protest at EU plans to eliminate national monopolies.

Meanwhile, public transport in the Normandy city of Rouen and the southern city of Toulouse was hit by strikes by workers pushing for shorter hours and a cut in retirement age to 55 from 60, a key concession to the truck drivers during their recent strike.
In Rouen, only about a tenth of 200 buses were running. In Toulouse, the local transport authority said 15 percent of buses were operating in a strike limited to morning services.

Three Elf Aquitaine refineries remained shut for a sixth day as strikers kept up a protest against cost savings and job cuts. Elf accused the workers of prolonging the strike with new demands, including retirement at 55.
Also threatened with job cuts, unions at Esso France, the French arm of U.S. oil major Exxon Corp, called for disruption including possible strikes at that firm's refineries on December 11-12.

The head of the Force Ouvriere (FO) union, Marc Blondel, said a cut in the retirement age for truckers, to 55 from 60 for drivers with 25 years' experience, had set an example for others after the crippling truckers' 12-day strike ended last Friday.
"That's created a precedent, and this precedent will help me and other unions. We'll be able to say that retirement is possible in difficult jobs at 55," Blondel told RMC radio.
He said the example would also help in public sector pay talks on winning better retirement deals.

Louis Viannet, leader of the Communist-led CGT union, said that the EDF-GDF strike showed workers were willing to fight with "demands that will continue to increase". He said there was "a climate of very, very strong discontent" in the country.
FO and the CGT spearheaded a crippling 24-day bout of public sector unrest late last year triggered by Prime Minister Alain Juppe's reforms of the creaking welfare system.
